text:
Predicates:
Twin(x) ::: x is a twin.
Triplet(x) ::: x is a triplet.
HangOut(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x) ::: x has siblings who are the same age.
Complains(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHome(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
StrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with their family members.
Premises:
∀x ((Twin(x) ∨ Triplet(x)) → HangOut(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (SameAgeSiblings(x) → (Twin(x) ∨ Triplet(x))) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (Complains(x) → SameAgeSiblings(x)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHome(x) → ¬StrongBonds(x)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x (HangOut(x) → ¬LiveAtHome(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
(Twin(luke) ∨ Triplet(luke)) ∧ StrongBonds(luke) ⊕ ¬(Twin(luke) ∨ Triplet(luke)) ∧ ¬StrongBonds(luke) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.
Conclusion:
HangOut(luke) ::: Luke spends a lot of time hanging out and playing with his siblings.
